details: Normalization and causal test

The comparable-profit bridge is 190 − 5 + 11 − 39 = 157. Segment profit contributions are NI +73, Mobile +65, Portfolio +7 and Group Common +12; this is a second decomposition, not an additional set of contributions. Total restructuring exclusions rose from 44 to 357, while acquisition amortization fell from 115 to 46. Total adjustments rose from 196 to 409, explaining why adjusted profit improves while statutory profit declines. Hedging was -16 versus +39, a EUR 55m headwind within operating results; removing it from both comparable periods gives 621/409 and a 47.2% diagnostic IOMA. That is not a fully normalized result because timing remains unquantified. Venture-fund gains are below operating profit and do not explain IOMA.
Revenue quality and historical premise

AI & Cloud sales were 631 versus 279, while telecom-provider sales were 3,640 versus 3,608. The former provides stronger growth evidence, but order intake is not recognized revenue and does not fix delivery timing. Use the recast Q1/Q2/Q3 series below: IOMA improves from Q2 but is below Q1, so it is not a monotonic acceleration. Earlier 2025 releases used different discontinued-operation and segment presentations; an unrecast Q3 2024 comparison would be misleading. Fully normalized current and prior revenue are n/a because the pull-forward amount is not disclosed.
Cash bridge and investing reconciliation

OCF change reconciles as pre-working-capital cash +109, working capital -619, net cash interest +5 and cash tax +3 = -502. Current working-capital flow is -563 versus +56; it cannot all be removed as temporary because inventory and receivables fund growth. Excluding working capital in BOTH periods produces a diagnostic 658/541 OCF and 464/373 FCF, not normalized cash. Other financial assets used 20/64 and generated 63/8, distinct from ordinary interest-bearing treasury investments. Investing cash is -281/-189, including acquisitions -30/-4, asset-sale proceeds +42/+9, treasury -145/+14, other-financial-asset net +43/-56 and remaining hedging/other +3/+16. Q3 operating cash includes discontinued-operation use -18/-21; adding this back gives a continuing-operations OCF diagnostic 113/618, still sharply down.
Reinvestment and contrary evidence

YTD OCF is 254/1,696. Gross cash investment is 476/458, so strict YTD FCF is -222/1,238; company FCF is -205/1,238 because it nets EUR 17m grants. Do not carry that grant netting into gross capex. Q3 capex intensity is 3.8%/3.6%. Management lowered full-year FCF conversion to 35–55%, plans another EUR 400m working-capital investment and expects EUR 800–900m restructuring cash outflows. Some manufacturing payments move into 2027; deferred capex is not a permanent saving.
Forward evidence and falsification

Management expects Q4 sales 20–24% above Q3 (calculated EUR 6,184.8–6,391.0m), and full-year comparable profit above the midpoint of EUR 2.1–2.6bn. It expects combined Optical and IP growth of 25–30% in 2027, not group growth of that magnitude. Q4 pull-forward reversal, AI-order conversion, receivables/inventory and actual restructuring payments are decisive tests. No comparable quarterly operating-profit guidance supports a forward IOMA calculation.

details: Accounting and normalization

GAAP consolidated operating income is the screen because adjusted refining income is only one segment. Applying only the company-identified refining operating adjustments to consolidated income creates an explicitly analyst-adjusted sensitivity: current 9,073−8=9,065; prior 1,509+50+5=1,564. IOMA is 7,501/13,930=53.8%, versus GAAP 54.3%. This removes known operating items in both years without pretending to be company consolidated adjusted operating income. The prior-year USD 1,131m impairment is a YTD item, not a Q3 expense, and is not added to Q3.
Mechanism and strongest contrary evidence

Refining margin per barrel rose from 13.14 to 39.24 despite throughput falling 3.7%. At 92 days, a diagnostic constant-volume decomposition of refining margin gives approximately +7,412.5m from margin-per-barrel and -415.2m from throughput, or +6,997.3m versus the disclosed +6,999m before costs; the 1.7m difference reflects rounded per-barrel metrics. This describes price/cost and mix, not durable pricing power. Refining operating D&A fell 148m, and operating expense fell 12m; neither is automatically a recurring productivity saving. Renewable diesel volume rose to 3.423m from 2.717m gallons/day, and ethanol to 4.799m from 4.635m. The completed St. Charles FCC optimization can improve product mix, but the release does not quantify its recurring contribution.
History and revenue normalization

GAAP IOMA rises versus Q2 2026. Q3 2025 had revenue down and profit up, producing a negative signed ratio despite favorable divergence; comparing ratio signs alone would invert the economic conclusion. Q1 2026 is distorted by the Q1 2025 impairment. No issuer constant-price revenue series is disclosed; do not label the 43.3% reported growth as normalized demand growth.
Cash normalization and investment scope

Working capital was -526 versus +325: a -851m drag on YoY OCF. Removing working-capital flows from BOTH periods gives diagnostic OCF 7,458/1,556, a +5,902m change; subtracting company investment figures gives 7,026/1,147. These are pre-working-capital diagnostics, not normalized FCF. Company adjusted OCF 7,253/1,642 also removes the other DGD owner’s share, so it is not consolidated OCF. Capital investment includes 162/232 of deferred turnarounds and catalyst payments, which must not be omitted as mere accounting amortization. Current components are 272−3+1+155+7=432; prior 171+4+2+187+45=409. The -3 DGD capex component needs the full filing to separate refunds/disposals from gross cash expenditure.
Cash trend, horizons and tests

YTD OCF is 13,902/3,769 and reported capital investments 1,230/1,476, giving a 12,672/2,293 cash-after-investment proxy. Latest available full filing is H1; Q3 treasury gross purchases, proceeds and remaining investing flows are not published in the release. No invented zero is used. A base case retains efficient operations but assumes commodity margins normalize; an adverse case combines lower spreads with outages or heavier turnaround spending. Monitor realized margin/barrel, utilization, DGD economics, deferred-turnaround cash and capex refunds. The release does not support numerical Q4 or FY2027 revenue/profit guidance or a forward IOMA.

Company organic revenue variance is +184 versus reported +166, with FX/divestiture/acquisition impact -18; adjusted-cost organic change is +70 versus reported +55, and organic profit change +114 versus +111. Index revenue grew 80 to 286; average ETP AUM rose to 1,108bn from 777bn, supported by flows AND market appreciation. FinTech revenue grew 72 to 529, with 54 new clients and 135 upsells. ARR of 3,365m is an annualized stock measure, not quarterly revenue.
Historical test

The four-quarter comparison below shows IOMA above Q3 2025 but below Q1/Q2 2026. Profitability remains strong without a claim of continuously accelerating conversion. Portfolio reclassifications altered gross revenue and segment presentation; consolidated net revenue and reconciled adjusted operating income are used throughout.
Cash, software and treasury limits

The Q3 2026 10-Q was not yet in the issuer’s SEC submissions retrieved for this run; latest full filing was H1. H1 OCF was 1,400/1,409 and disclosed PP&E purchases 137/108, giving 1,263/1,301 cash-after-PP&E. Current Q3 securities flows and the full investing reconciliation remain unavailable. Management updated FY2026 adjusted expense guidance to 2,550–2,580: subtracting nine-month 1,887 implies Q4 expense of 663–693, a calculation rather than profit guidance. ARR supports Q4 fee growth, but a market drawdown can reverse index fees, while higher staffing and technology costs can reduce incremental conversion. Monitor retention, organic ARR, index flows versus appreciation and the forthcoming cash-flow statement.

details: GAAP, adjusted and normalization

GAAP operating profit is 162.253/71.906, versus adjusted 208.996/92.547. GAAP IOMA is 20.0%; adjusted IOMA is 25.8%. Current operating exclusions total 46.743: intangible amortization 9.224, SBC 24.090, unrealized commodity-hedge gain -0.516, restructuring/acquisition/other 13.945. Prior exclusions total 20.641: 9.225+11.611−0.776+0.581. The 26.102 increase in exclusions explains the extra adjusted profit growth. Retaining SBC in BOTH adjusted periods gives analyst profit 184.906/80.936 and IOMA 23.0%; the screen itself remains the company basis. Adjusted EBITDA of 242.307/120.915 is a different measure and is not substituted for operating income.
Demand, acquisitions and history

Commercial segment sales rose from 408.920 to 787.882; A&D from 344.482 to 416.540, before eliminations. Management reports data-center/networking growth of 115%, medical/industrial/instrumentation 97% and A&D 21%. Book-to-bill of 2.13 and A&D backlog of 2.0bn support demand but are not guaranteed quarterly sales. Epiq closed September 30, after the September 28 fiscal-quarter end; do not attribute Q3 growth to its full future contribution. A precise acquisition-free two-period sales bridge is not disclosed, so normalized organic growth is n/a. The same-basis Q1–Q3 2026 YoY series shows higher IOMA in Q3. The older Q3 2025 release lacked the same adjusted-operating-income reconciliation, so its EBITDA is not spliced into that series.
Cash conversion and investing

OCF/adjusted operating profit fell from 153.2% to 74.0%; OCF/revenue fell from 18.8% to 12.9%. This is a material divergence even though cash grew. Company FCF increase reconciles exactly as OCF +12.908 plus reduced net capex +19.312 = +32.220. YTD OCF is 272.883/228.952 and company net capex 237.138/222.687, producing company FCF 35.745/6.265. The H1 filing shows purchases 169.205/123.726 and asset-sale proceeds 11.988/0.272, which demonstrates why net capex cannot be described as gross investment. Prior Q3 purchases are 223.176−123.726=99.450, and proceeds 0.489−0.272=0.217. Current-quarter disposal proceeds, separately capitalized software, securities investing and acquisition cash classification are unavailable in the release. Do not use the USD 650m announced Ophir purchase price as cash already spent.
Capital burden and cash normalization

Net-capex/revenue is 6.6%/13.2%; lower net spending is not evidence that required maintenance investment permanently fell. H1 unpaid PP&E in payables was 140.132m, a noncash addition that can become later cash demand. The current quarter’s inventory, receivables, customer deposits, cash tax and capex-payable bridge is not available, so normalized OCF/FCF is n/a for both periods rather than assuming all working capital reverses. Announced acquisitions and facility ramps create additional integration and funding demands.
Forward scenarios and falsification

Management guides Q4 sales to 1,420–1,440m, FY2026 to 4,470–4,490m and preliminary FY2027 to 6,500–6,750m. The latter implies roughly 45–51% growth across range endpoints, but includes closed STG/Epiq and is not organic guidance. Proposed Ophir, Merlin and ILFA transactions are excluded as stated in the release. EPS guidance cannot be converted to operating income without an unsupported bridge. Base case retains strong AI/A&D shipments with cost investment; adverse case combines customer acceptance delays, acquisition integration and collection/capex catch-up. Watch realized backlog conversion, margins retaining SBC, cash collections and gross capex.

Revenue normalization and demand

Reported revenue is 243.825/182.313. Copra contributed 16.0 percentage points of growth in the company’s rounded reconciliation, implying approximately 29.17m acquired sales and approximately 214.65m ex-Copra current sales against 182.313m prior sales. Branded coconut-water case-equivalent volume grew 16%, while branded revenue grew about 15%; private-label volumes grew 77% but revenue grew 152%, illustrating acquisition/mix effects. Price-volume interactions are not double-counted as additive growth drivers.
Cash bridge and normalization

Quarter cash is derived consistently: OCF 151.942−96.529=55.413 versus 51.069−12.010=39.059; capex 0.803−0.612=0.191 versus 4.921−1.508=3.413. The +16.354 OCF bridge comprises net income +11.014, receivables +9.737, inventory +5.379, prepaids/advances -1.860, payables/accruals -13.943 and noncash/other +6.027. These sum to +16.354; the +3.222 reduction in capex then yields +19.576 FCF. Receivable collections and inventory release are helpful, but cannot automatically be removed as temporary or counted as indefinitely recurring. Keeping all disclosed working-capital flows is the primary result; normalized OCF/FCF remains n/a because cash timing of refunds and acquisition effects is not isolated.
Investment burden and history

Capex intensity is only 0.08%/1.87% of sales, consistent with an asset-light model but not evidence of zero future supply-chain investment. No separate software/development capitalization line is reported in the released statements. YTD FCF is 151.139/46.148. IOMA improves versus Q3 2025 but falls sharply from Q2 2026, when tariff economics aided the comparison. TTM normalization is incomplete without Q4 data on a consistent acquisition perimeter.
Guidance and adverse case

FY2026 sales guidance is 810–820m and EBITDA 170–175m. Management expects Q4 gross margin near 33%, below Q3’s 38%, with higher costs and no price offsets until early 2027. This directly argues against extrapolating Q3 conversion. The next-year base case assumes category growth continues but must fund freight/input inflation; the adverse case adds private-label dilution and price elasticity. Watch ex-Copra growth, gross margin, tariffs, receivable days and realized 2027 price increases.

Tungsten, savings and underlying demand

Machining disclosed SEK 104m temporary tungsten-price timing benefit and SEK 82m savings. Group FX contributed +158m to EBITA. These are overlapping with the gross-profit/segment bridges and must not be added again. The unquantified price-driven powder gain and pre-buying could be more material than the disclosed timing item. A precise durable share of the remaining profit is therefore n/a.
Revenue bridge and history

Profit and revenue now both grow; the older positive ratio reflected both shrinking, not superior economics.

Investing reconciliation and durability

Their nature and the other-investment composition need fuller notes. Do not compare these different definitions as if they were the same FCF.
